solution:
[Textbook answer-key error: the printed key gives "SSC Test", which names no test this chapter teaches. The four congruence tests introduced here are side-side-side, side-angle-side, angle-side-angle and hypotenuse-side, and the intended answer is plainly the first of them: the figure marks all THREE pairs of corresponding sides congruent (one tick on AB and PQ, two on BC and QR, three on AC and PR) and marks no angle anywhere, so side-side-side is the only test that applies. It is a one-letter misprint, the final S set as a C. Confirmed off the printed answer page at 3x magnification, where the third glyph is an open C, clearly distinct from the two closed-loop S's before it and from the "SAS Test" printed immediately to its right. The remaining three parts of this same key entry are correct.]

The marks show all three pairs of corresponding sides congruent: seg AB \(\cong\) seg PQ (one tick), seg BC \(\cong\) seg QR (two ticks) and seg AC \(\cong\) seg PR (three ticks). Three pairs of congruent sides give congruence by the side-side-side test.
By SSS test, \(\triangle ABC \cong \triangle PQR\).

The marks show seg XY \(\cong\) seg LM, \(\angle Y \cong \angle M\) and seg YZ \(\cong\) seg MN. The congruent angles lie between the two pairs of congruent sides, so this is the side-angle-side test.
By SAS test, \(\triangle XYZ \cong \triangle LMN\).

The marks show \(\angle P \cong \angle S\), seg PR \(\cong\) seg ST and \(\angle R \cong \angle T\). The congruent sides lie between the two pairs of congruent angles, so this is the angle-side-angle test.
By ASA test, \(\triangle PRQ \cong \triangle STU\).

\(\angle M\) and \(\angle T\) are right angles, so seg LN and seg PR are the hypotenuses, and they are marked congruent; the sides seg LM and seg PT are also marked congruent. Two right angled triangles with congruent hypotenuses and one pair of congruent remaining sides are congruent by the hypotenuse-side test.
By hypotenuse-side test, \(\triangle LMN \cong \triangle PTR\).

The congruent side BC lies between the congruent angles \(\angle ABC\) and \(\angle ACB\), and the congruent side QR lies between \(\angle PQR\) and \(\angle PRQ\), so the triangles are congruent by the angle-side-angle test.
\(\therefore \triangle ABC \cong \triangle PQR\) ..... ASA test.
The correspondence is A - P, B - Q, C - R, so the remaining parts are:
\(\therefore \angle BAC \cong \angle QPR\) (corresponding angles of congruent triangles).
seg AB \(\cong\) seg PQ and seg AC \(\cong\) seg PR (corresponding sides of congruent triangles).

The congruent angles \(\angle PTQ\) and \(\angle STR\) lie between the congruent sides seg PT, seg TQ and seg ST, seg TR respectively, so the triangles are congruent by the side-angle-side test.
\(\therefore \triangle PTQ \cong \triangle STR\) ..... SAS test.
The correspondence is P - S, T - T, Q - R, so the remaining parts are:
\(\therefore \angle TPQ \cong \angle TSR\) and \(\angle TQP \cong \angle TRS\) (corresponding angles of congruent triangles).
seg PQ \(\cong\) seg SR (corresponding sides of congruent triangles).

\(\angle A\) and \(\angle Q\) are right angles, so seg BC and seg PR are the hypotenuses of the two triangles, and they are marked congruent. The sides seg AB and seg PQ are also marked congruent. Two right angled triangles with congruent hypotenuses and one pair of congruent remaining sides are congruent by the hypotenuse-side test.
Matching the right angle at A with the right angle at Q, the hypotenuse BC with the hypotenuse PR, and the side AB with the side QP, the correspondence is A - Q, B - P, C - R.
\(\therefore \triangle ABC \cong \triangle QPR\) ..... hypotenuse-side test.
The remaining congruent parts are seg AC \(\cong\) seg QR (corresponding sides of congruent triangles), and \(\angle ABC \cong \angle QPR\), \(\angle ACB \cong \angle QRP\) (corresponding angles of congruent triangles).

In \(\triangle LMN\) and \(\triangle PNM\):
seg LM \(\cong\) seg PN (given),
seg LN \(\cong\) seg PM (given),
seg MN \(\cong\) seg NM (common side).
All three pairs of corresponding sides are congruent.
\(\therefore \triangle LMN \cong \triangle PNM\) ..... SSS test.
The correspondence is L - P, M - N, N - M, so the remaining congruent parts are \(\angle LMN \cong \angle PNM\), \(\angle LNM \cong \angle PMN\) and \(\angle MLN \cong \angle NPM\) (corresponding angles of congruent triangles).

In \(\triangle ABD\) and \(\triangle CBD\):
seg AB \(\cong\) seg CB (given),
seg AD \(\cong\) seg CD (given),
seg BD \(\cong\) seg BD (common side).
All three pairs of corresponding sides are congruent, so by the SSS test \(\triangle ABD \cong \triangle CBD\).

The point T lies on side QR, so ray QT is the same ray as ray QR; and the point S lies on side QP, so ray QS is the same ray as ray QP. Hence \(\angle PQT\) and \(\angle RQS\) are both the angle \(\angle PQR\), and so \(\angle PQT \cong \angle RQS\).
In \(\triangle PQT\) and \(\triangle RQS\):
\(\angle QPT \cong \angle QRS\) (given, \(\angle P \cong \angle R\)),
seg PQ \(\cong\) seg RQ (given),
\(\angle PQT \cong \angle RQS\) (shown above, the common angle at Q).
The congruent sides lie between the two pairs of congruent angles, so by the ASA test \(\triangle PQT \cong \triangle RQS\).
